title: Lifting an embedded have into a private lemma (strict-monotone bound)
intent: Take the `have hk_bound` embedded in a long proof, promote its surrounding context (`m'`, `k`, `hk_mono`) into explicit parameters, and generalise the specific bound `k i ≤ k ⟨m', Nat.lt_succ_self m'⟩` to `k i ≤ k last`, so the main proof closes its strict bound `k i < n` by `omega` from a top-level `private lemma` instead of an inline calculation.

parent.name: hk_bound
parent.statement: have hk_bound : ∀ i : Fin (m' + 1), k i < n := by

children.name: strictMono_all_lt_succ_last
children.statement: private lemma strictMono_all_lt_succ_last {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ℕ) (hk : StrictMono k) (i : Fin m) (last : Fin m) (h_last : ∀ j, j ≤ last) : k i ≤ k last
children.closed_by: apply StrictMono.monotone hk; exact h_last i

applicability.goal_shape: An embedded `have` (or `assert`) inside a long proof whose conclusion uses proof-local context; the reusable content is a monotonicity fact of the form `k i ≤ k last` obtained by `StrictMono.monotone`, stated with proof-specific constants (`n`, `m'`, the last index `⟨m', Nat.lt_succ_self m'⟩`).
applicability.use_when: the embedded fact has independent mathematical content that can be re-stated with the surrounding context promoted to parameters; the fact is reusable or would shorten and clarify the main proof; the file's own triggers apply (a large preliminary calculation, or a bound whose only proof-specific part is the choice of last index).
applicability.avoid_when: the fact would need many parameters (the file warns against 10+ / 15+ parameter helpers); the statement depends on definitional `let` bindings (Pattern 2.3, measure theory); the `have` is short, linear and used once with no independent meaning; or the extraction would obscure the main flow.

claims.claim: The embedded `have hk_bound` closes with `omega` (line 316), after an inner `have : k i ≤ k ⟨m', Nat.lt_succ_self m'⟩` closed by `apply StrictMono.monotone hk_mono; exact Fin.le_last i` (lines 313-315), with `simp only [n]` discharging the `n` of the outer goal.

The extracted `private lemma strictMono_all_lt_succ_last` closes with the same two-step argument `apply StrictMono.monotone hk; exact h_last i` (lines 326-327), where the specific last index `⟨m', Nat.lt_succ_self m'⟩` and the witness `Fin.le_last i` of the inner `have` become the parameters `last : Fin m` and `h_last : ∀ j, j ≤ last`.

The authors state the extracted lemma's meaning in its docstring, 'Strictly monotone functions satisfy k(i) ≤ k(last) for all i' (line 321), and the point of the extraction in prose, 'Result: Main proof now just calls helper, much clearer.' (line 330).

The same file states the recipe this example follows, 'Copy have proof to new lemma; Identify required parameters; Replace original with have h := helper args' (lines 264-266), and the generalisation step is its own rule, 'Generic is better (Pattern 2.1): Remove proof-specific constraints' (line 39).

metrics.how_counted: parent = lines 310-316 of the copied file (the before `have` block); child = lines 321-327 (the extracted lemma); the lemma takes one implicit parameter `{m : ℕ}` plus five explicit parameters `(k, hk, i, last, h_last)`.

consequences: The extracted lemma must carry the whole context as parameters: `m'` in `Fin (m' + 1)` is re-typed as the implicit `{m : ℕ}`, `k` and `hk_mono` become `k` and `hk : StrictMono k`, and the specific last index `⟨m', Nat.lt_succ_self m'⟩` is generalised to `last : Fin m` with the explicit hypothesis `h_last : ∀ j, j ≤ last` (previously supplied for free by `Fin.le_last i`). The outer `have hk_bound` is then closed by `omega` from the helper, so the caller must still supply the `last`/`h_last` pair and finish the strict bound. A helper left too specific (still naming `n` and `m'`) would not be reusable; one made too general gains a hypothesis the caller must discharge. The file's Pattern 5.1 requires recompiling after each such extraction, since a parameter mismatch or a dropped hypothesis is caught only by the compiler.
